A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CiteBART study and support comparison of the complete main text and appendices. Tables, equations, and appendix figures are readable; relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative citation-generation experiments in Tables 4–6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds hallucination measurements in Tables 7–8 and further qualitative examples in Tables 5 and 9.

M1.justification: Both versions use BART-base with masked author-date citations, the same Base and Global input schemes, and the same decoding procedure. The added hallucination metrics analyze outputs without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: The four datasets and LCR task remain unchanged. v2 adds limited transfer scenarios: an Arxiv-trained model predicts a shared citation from an unseen PeerRead context, supplementing v1's transfer example with an unseen target citation, and Table 9 adds an ACL-200-to-Refseer case.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains BERT-GCN on PeerRead, DualEnh-ws on ACL-200 and Refseer, and HAtten on all four benchmarks. The Llama-2-70b-chat appendix experiments also remain unchanged. Newly cited generation systems are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 introduces a substantial hallucination-evaluation protocol: citation-list membership checking, top-3/5/10 analyses, subtype rates, and measurements conditional on ground-truth matches. Existing split sizes, training budgets, and decoding settings remain unchanged; removing the explicit 8:2 wording does not establish a changed split.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic hallucination error analysis, sensitivity to prediction-list length, and analysis of hallucination conditional on successful prediction. It also adds one transfer example to Table 5 and six cases in Table 9. The four original component ablations and appendix LLM examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports p < 0.001 for differences between MaHR and its match-conditioned variants. v1 provides no numerical significance levels. The added statement does not specify the statistical test, and neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: All benchmark and ablation scores in Tables 4 and 6 remain unchanged. New Tables 7–8 provide substantial additional results: top-3 MaHR is 4.12%, 8.02%, 5.28%, and 4.64% for ACL-200, PeerRead, Refseer, and Arxiv, respectively. Arxiv's top-10 MaHR is 13.35%, versus 6.28% and 3.95% under the two match conditions. Additional qualitative predictions are also reported.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 adds formal hallucination-metric definitions and decompositions, including the equality of MaHR and MiHR when every context receives the same number of predictions. These are limited mathematical additions, without new theorems or proofs. The existing MRR definition is merely relocated.

C1.justification: The method and benchmark-superiority claims remain, but v2 substantially expands the stated contributions to include hallucination taxonomy and quantitative behavior. The headline zero-shot claim is reframed as cross-dataset generalization, alongside new claims of 4% top-3 MaHR and reduced hallucination when the correct citation appears.

C2.justification: v2 develops interpretations connecting partial author/year matches to useful reading suggestions and potential zero-shot capability, and successful prediction to lower hallucination. It removes the explicit limitations concerning assumed citation-worthiness, omission of papers or authors outside the training corpus, and bias toward citing-paper information. Hallucination itself remains extensively discussed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a pretrained-model download link while retaining code and dataset access information. It removes the explicit explanation of constructing an 8:2 split and replacing three partitions with two, although Table 3 is unchanged. Hyperparameters, hardware, token limits, and timing information remain the same.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fierro et al. (2024) and Gao et al. (2023, ALCE) to distinguish LCR from generating answers or summaries with citations, and Li et al. (2024) for hallucination metrics. Jurgens et al. (2018) and Vaswani et al. (2017) are removed; the main LCR positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, condenses introductory and related-work background, moves the unchanged metrics appendix into Section 3.3, and reorganizes concluding material. These are localized editorial and structural revisions within the retained overall organization; most method and original experimental exposition remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds two quantitative hallucination tables and a large case-study table with highlighted errors. Table 5 gains a fourth example and an example-dataset column, while Tables 4 and 6 are reformatted. Appendix Figures 1–2 are identical, and the token-limit table is retained as Table 10.

improvement.justification: The added dataset-relative hallucination measurements and examples provide a modest net gain over v1's largely anecdotal treatment of this failure mode; pretrained-model access also helps reproducibility. The gain is limited by removing explicit limitations and split-construction wording, unspecified testing behind p < 0.001, and the abstract's unqualified 4% claim despite Table 7's top-3 rates ranging from 4.12% to 8.02%.
